fund_004:n1.prompt:
You are helping me verify that our 409A valuation is current before we issue new stock options to team members. Please do the following:

1. If you don't already have it, ask me for our {{vendor}} issuer ID and confirm you can use my configured credentials to access the {{vendor}} API/dashboard.
2. Using the {{vendor}} API (the fair-market-values endpoint that retrieves the issuer's fair market values from its 409A valuations), pull the current 409A valuation record(s) for our company, including the valuation date, expiration date, and fair market value per share.
3. Determine whether the valuation is still "current" — typically valid for 12 months from the valuation date, or less if a material event (financing round, major business change) has occurred since. Flag clearly if it has expired or is expiring within the next 30 days.
4. If the valuation is stale or about to expire, check whether {{vendor}} supports ordering a new audit-ready 409A valuation in-platform generated from our live cap table, and prepare a summary of what that would involve (data it will use, estimated turnaround) — but do not initiate a purchase or submit any order; that remains a human step.
5. Cross-check the valuation's underlying cap table snapshot against our current cap table (stakeholders, share classes, vesting states) via {{vendor}}'s API to confirm no major discrepancies exist that would call the valuation into question.

When done, report back to me with: (a) whether the 409A is currently valid, (b) the valuation amount and expiration date, (c) any discrepancies found in the underlying cap table, and (d) if a refresh is needed, a prepared summary/checklist for ordering a new valuation so I can review and stop for human sign-off before proceeding with any purchase or grant.

fund_004:n2.prompt:
You are helping me draft a Board Consent (Unanimous Written Consent in Lieu of Meeting) approving new stock option grants, as part of our stock option issuance process. This is a document-preparation task only — no filing or execution.

First, ask me for any missing details: (1) legal company name and state of incorporation, (2) current equity incentive plan name and adoption date (e.g., '2021 Equity Incentive Plan'), (3) list of grantees with title/role, number of shares/options per grantee, exercise (strike) price per share, vesting schedule (e.g., 4-year with 1-year cliff), and grant date, (4) names of all current board members and the date the consent will circulate, (5) whether a 409A valuation is current and its effective date, and (6) whether option agreements will be countersigned in Carta or another cap table system.

Using this information, draft a complete Board Consent document containing: recitals referencing the equity plan and 409A valuation, resolved clauses approving each individual grant with share count, strike price, vesting terms, and authorizing officers to execute option agreements and record the grants in our cap table system, plus a signature block for each board member.

Also prepare a short checklist listing: the draft consent, the grantee/grant details table, and next steps (circulate to board, collect signatures, then record grants and issue option agreements once approved).

Do not send, distribute, or submit this consent to the board, and do not mark any grant as approved — stop for human sign-off. Report back with the drafted consent text, the grant summary table, and the checklist for my review.

fund_004:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the board consent for approving new stock option grants (Process: Issue Stock Options, step fund_004:n3). This is a policy-gate step: the board itself must review and sign — you must prepare everything but stop for human sign-off.

If missing, ask me for: (1) the list of grantees with name, title, number of options, exercise price, vesting schedule, and grant date for each; (2) the equity incentive plan name/date it falls under; (3) the current option pool availability if known; (4) our company's legal name and state of incorporation; (5) the names of current board members/directors who must sign; (6) any prior board consent template or corporate records tool (e.g., Carta, a document management system, or email) we use to circulate consents.

Actions to take:
1. Draft a Unanimous Written Consent of the Board of Directors (or equivalent action-by-written-consent document) approving the option grants, referencing the equity incentive plan, listing each grantee with their grant details, and confirming sufficient shares remain reserved in the option pool.
2. Prepare a clean checklist summarizing: grantees, share counts, strike prices, vesting terms, plan reference, and any required exhibits (e.g., option agreement templates).
3. Draft a short cover note/email I can send to board members explaining what they're being asked to approve and sign, with instructions for returning signed copies.
4. Do NOT send this for signature, submit it anywhere, or mark it approved — only prepare the draft consent, checklist, and cover note.

When done, report back: the draft consent text, the checklist of grant details, the draft cover note, and a clear note that this must stop for human sign-off before the board actually signs. Flag any missing information you need from me before finalizing the draft.

fund_004:n4.prompt:
You are helping me generate a stock option agreement for a new grant using {{vendor}}, our equity-management platform. Before starting, ask me for: (1) the recipient's name and role, (2) the number of options to grant, (3) the vesting schedule details (standard 4-year/1-year cliff, custom milestones, or acceleration terms), (4) the strike price or confirmation to use the current 409A-compliant fair market value on file, and (5) my {{vendor}} issuer ID if not already configured in your credentials.

Once you have these inputs, use your configured {{vendor}} credentials to create a draft option grant via the platform's programmatic surface (the equivalent of {{vendor}}'s draft option grant creation endpoint, e.g. POST /v1alpha1/issuers/{issuerId}/draftSecurities/optionGrants), populating recipient details, grant quantity, vesting schedule, and strike price exactly as specified. Configure any custom vesting terms (cliffs, milestone triggers, exit acceleration) so the platform can track vested vs. unvested shares automatically.

Do not submit the grant for board approval or finalize it — leave it in draft/pending status queued for board review, since board consent is required before this option agreement takes effect. Prepare a clear summary of the draft grant (recipient, quantity, vesting terms, strike price, and a link or reference ID to the draft in {{vendor}}) for my review.

Report back with this summary and confirmation that the draft is queued in {{vendor}}, then stop for human sign-off — I will personally review and route it through board approval.

fund_004:n5.prompt:
You are helping me complete step fund_004:n5 in our stock-option issuance process: send the finalized option agreement to the employee for e-signature using {{vendor}}, our legal-ops/e-signature platform.

Before acting, ask me for anything you don't already have: (1) the employee's full legal name and email, (2) the finalized option agreement document or template (including grant details: number of shares, strike price, vesting schedule, board approval date), and (3) confirmation that {{vendor}} is already connected with configured credentials.

Actions to take:
1. Using {{vendor}}'s document/e-signature capabilities, populate the option agreement template with the employee's details and grant terms.
2. Set up the signature routing so the document is sent to the employee (and any co-signers such as the company officer, if required) in the correct signing order.
3. Prepare the send — recipient list, document content, and routing — but do NOT actually dispatch it for signature yet.
4. Compile a summary showing: employee name, grant terms populated into the document, signer routing order, and a preview/link to the prepared document for my review.

Because this step requires explicit human approval before changes are applied, you must not send, finalize, or trigger the signature request yourself. Once everything is prepared and verified for accuracy, present it to me and stop for human sign-off — I will review and give the final go-ahead to send it myself through {{vendor}}.

Report back with: the recipient(s) and routing order, a summary of the populated grant terms, a link or reference to the prepared document in {{vendor}}, and a clear note that the send action is pending my approval and has not been executed.

fund_004:n6.prompt:
You are helping me record a stock option grant on {{vendor}}, our equity management platform, as part of our 'Issue stock options' process. This step must stop short of finalizing anything, since a human must explicitly approve the grant before it takes effect.

Please ask me for any of the following you don't already have: my {{vendor}} issuer ID, the recipient's name/employee ID, number of options granted, strike price (per our latest 409A valuation), vesting schedule/start date, grant date, and confirmation that board approval for this specific grant is either already obtained or pending.

Using my configured credentials, create a draft option grant via {{vendor}}'s programmatic API (issuers/{issuerId}/draft-securities/option-grants endpoint) with the details provided, so it is queued as a draft awaiting board approval — do not attempt to finalize, approve, or submit it for board sign-off yourself. This step remains a human step: the actual board approval and finalization of the grant must be done by a human.

Once the draft is created, prepare a short summary for me listing: recipient, share count, strike price, vesting terms, and the draft's status/ID as returned by {{vendor}}. Do not attempt to verify the grant on the live cap table yet (via the option-grants retrieval endpoint) until after I confirm board approval has occurred — flag that as the next step.

Report back with the draft grant details, its current status in {{vendor}}, and a clear note that this task must now stop for human sign-off before the grant is approved and reflected on the cap table.
